caption: We've never combined our accounts before this. Would you actually want to see your partner's full budget?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R30 800
household income
Living in Worcester
slides.body:
Him 26, her 25
Living together, not married
Jobs: Farm production assistant & ECD teacher
Combined net: R30 800 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 3 bed cottage outside town, water, refuse
slides.body: Neither of us could have afforded this alone. Together it still felt like a jump.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers big shop, Spar top-ups, his protein shakes
slides.body: We shop together now. It hasn't made the trolley any cheaper.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: His bakkie, needed for the farm roads
slides.body: Her car sits at her mom's. His bakkie is the only one that gets us both to work.

slides.title: Petrol & insurance
slides.includes: Farm roads and the daily run into town
slides.body: The dirt roads eat tyres faster than either of us expected.

slides.title: Takeaways & Friday drinks
slides.includes: Friday night out, the odd delivery when neither of us can face cooking
slides.body: We guessed R600 between us. It's R1 400. Neither of us wants to be the one who admits that first.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, phone & fibre, both funeral policies, a stokvel he's in, black tax to both families, savings
slides.body: Twelve thousand rand of things we'd only ever budgeted for separately before this.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R30 800 between us. First time we've actually seen the whole picture side by side.

slides.title: We stopped guessing about each other's numbers
slides.body:
We put both our statements into Beyond Horizon and split the budget by category for the first time.

Neither of us knew the other was still paying black tax to two households until we saw it on one screen.

No bank login needed.
